package_info.why_malicious: The package is a brandjacking/typosquatting attack imitating the popular 'browserify' package. It contains a malicious postinstall script that extracts and executes a large ELF binary ('run') which performs privilege escalation, system destruction, persistence, extensive system fingerprinting, and data exfiltration. The package is specifically crafted to evade detection and targets NodeJS developers on Linux and Mac.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Runs a NodeJS script (postinstall.js) to extract a tar.xz archive, executes the extracted ELF binary ('run'), and deletes the temporary directory.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts that execute binaries and clean up traces are a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely execute native binaries or delete files during postinstall.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may use postinstall for native module compilation, but not for arbitrary binary execution.
key_indicators: Executes a bundled binary during install

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Decompresses a tar.xz archive containing the malicious ELF binary.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Extracting and running hidden binaries is a classic malware technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal postinstall scripts do not extract and execute large, opaque binaries.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
systemctl stop .service
systemctl disable
rm -rf /etc/systemd/system/
rm -rf /etc/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attempts to stop system services, disable them, and delete critical system directories including /etc/systemd/system/ and /etc/.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Destructive commands targeting system configuration and service management are highly malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should attempt to delete /etc or disable system services.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Gains persistence by copying itself to a system directory to run on every boot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence mechanisms in system directories are a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not self-replicate to /etc/ for persistence.

execution_context.file_location: bin/run/run (ELF binary, uses bundled 'sudo-prompt' npm module)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Uses 'sudo-prompt' to request admin privileges via GUI prompt
malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (via NodeJS module in ELF binary)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Displays a cross-platform prompt to the user to obtain root/admin credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often uses social engineering to escalate privileges.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require admin rights immediately after install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers request admin rights, but not via postinstall scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Collects system info (OS, username, CPU/GPU, docker images, Bluetooth devices, etc.)
malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (via NodeJS module in ELF binary)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Performs extensive fingerprinting and reconnaissance of the infected system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reconnaissance and fingerprinting are common in targeted attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not collect and exfiltrate such broad system data.
key_indicators: Enumeration of hardware, software, and user data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Exfiltrates collected system information to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Frequent outbound connections to suspicious domains for data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not exfiltrate user/system data to external servers.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package, triggering the postinstall script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extraction and execution of the malicious ELF binary.

attack_chain.action: postinstall.js extracts the run.tar.xz archive to reveal the ELF binary.
The ELF binary ('run') executes, immediately requesting admin privileges via a GUI prompt.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation if the user grants access.

attack_chain.action: With elevated privileges, the binary attempts to stop and disable system services, and deletes critical system directories.
The binary copies itself to /etc/rot1 for persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ensures malware runs on every boot.

attack_chain.action: Performs extensive system fingerprinting and reconnaissance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of sensitive system and user data.

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrates collected data to a remote server via HTTP.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives system data; attack complete.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall scripts that execute or extract native binaries
Immediate privilege escalation requests after install
Destructive commands targeting /etc/ or systemd directories
Persistence via self-copy to /etc/ or similar system directories
Frequent outbound HTTP connections to non-standard domains
file_indicators: Presence of run.tar.xz or large ELF binaries in npm packages
Temporary extraction and deletion of binary payloads during install
network_indicators: HTTP requests to me.ejemplo.me or similar suspicious domains
Regular outbound connections immediately after install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that extract and execute native binaries, especially those that request admin privileges. Flag packages containing large, opaque ELF binaries or archives. Detect destructive commands targeting /etc/ or systemd directories. Watch for persistence mechanisms involving self-copy to system directories. Alert on frequent outbound HTTP connections to non-standard or suspicious domains, especially following package installation. Use static and dynamic analysis to inspect bundled binaries for embedded reconnaissance and exfiltration logic.
